what.text: IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 IGF-I) is a man-made version of human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). It has an extra chain of amino acids added at the start, and the third amino acid is changed from glutamate to arginine (the “R3”).

src.label: Tomas FM, et al. J Endocrinol 1993

what.text: These changes make it bind about 1,000 times less strongly to the IGF binding proteins that normally hold IGF-1 in the blood. In rats it was cleared from the blood faster than IGF-1, yet it was about six times more potent at increasing growth.

src.label: Ballard FJ, et al. Growth Regul 1993

what.text: It is used mainly in cell culture and animal research. It is not the same as mecasermin (Increlex), the FDA-approved IGF-1 medicine, which has the same 70-amino-acid sequence as the body’s own IGF-1.

what.text: IGF-1 LR3 has never been tested in a published human study.

research.text: No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. All research on IGF-1 LR3 is in animals and cells. A 2026 review of growth-hormone-related peptides found no peer-reviewed human studies.
No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026.

research.title: Growth in normal female rats, 1993

facts.v: animal study comparing IGF-1 and IGF-1 LR3 given by pump under the skin
weight gain, nitrogen retention, food efficiency and organ weights

research.found: Both raised weight gain and nitrogen retention. IGF-1 LR3 did so at a much lower dose than IGF-1.

src.label: Tomas FM, et al. J Endocrinol 1993

research.title: Growth-restricted fetal sheep, 2025

facts.v: controlled animal study, IGF-1 LR3 or vehicle infused into the fetus
14 growth-restricted sheep fetuses late in pregnancy (7 per group)
fetal weight, insulin, glucose and amino acids

research.found: IGF-1 LR3 did not improve fetal growth. Blood amino acids fell.

src.label: White A, et al. Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 2025

research.text: In 2010, a doping lab analyzed an injection vial from the black market and found IGF-1 LR3 with a laboratory purification tag (a His-tag) still attached. The authors said the effects of this tagged form in humans have never been described and the product was likely a by-product of lab research.

src.label: Kohler M, et al. Growth Horm IGF Res 2010

us.text: IGF-1 LR3 is not FDA approved for any use. It is sold online as a “research compound.” FDA does not allow unapproved drugs labelled for research to be sold for human use. The approved IGF-1 drug, mecasermin (Increlex), is a different product. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none for IGF-1 LR3. It does not appear on FDA’s 503A nomination category lists or its Category 2 safety-risk page.

items.text: FDA has said that companies selling unapproved drugs “falsely labeled ‘for research purposes’ or ‘not for human consumption’” have sold them illegally, when the products are sold to consumers for human use. FDA made this statement about GLP-1 drugs.

src.label: FDA, concerns with unapproved GLP-1 drugs (section on products sold "for research purposes")

items.text: Increlex (mecasermin), approved by FDA in 2005 (BLA 021839), is recombinant human IGF-1 with the natural sequence. It is approved only for growth failure in children aged 2 and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, or with growth hormone gene deletion and antibodies to growth hormone. It is not a substitute for growth hormone. Any other use is off-label.

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

world.lead: No regulator has approved IGF-1 LR3. Mecasermin (Increlex), a different IGF-1 drug, is approved in the US, Canada, the EU and Australia for rare growth disorders in children. Australia lists insulin-like growth factors as prescription-only and illegal to possess without authority.

countries.status: IGF-1 LR3 not approved. Mecasermin (Increlex) approved 2005 for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency in children.
IGF-1 LR3 not in the Drug Product Database. Increlex (mecasermin) is listed as marketed. Health Canada says peptides are generally regulated as prescription drugs.

after.text: IGF-1 LR3 is prohibited at all times under class S2.3 of the 2026 Prohibited List, which names “Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1, mecasermin) and its analogues.” IGF-1 LR3 is an IGF-1 analogue. S2 substances are not “specified substances.” The 2027 list keeps the entry.

side.text: No human safety data exist for IGF-1 LR3. The approved IGF-1 drug, Increlex, shows what IGF-1 itself can do; IGF-1 LR3 is more potent in animals, and its effects in people are unknown.

items.text: no peer-reviewed human studies; a 2026 review notes a theoretical risk of promoting cell growth, based on IGF-1 signaling biology.

src.label: Dominikowski A, et al. Front Endocrinol 2026 (review)

items.text: severe low blood sugar, including seizures; allergic reactions including anaphylaxis; raised pressure in the skull; enlarged tonsils; hip joint problems (slipped capital femoral epiphysis); worsening scoliosis; and cases of cancer in treated children. Increlex is contraindicated in children with cancer or a history of cancer.

surprises: In rats, IGF-1 LR3 left the blood faster than natural IGF-1 but was about six times more potent, because it escapes the binding proteins that normally restrain IGF-1.
